newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodia says ASEAN interference not welcome.
newsitem.headline: Cambodia says ASEAN interference not welcome.

text.p: Cambodian Foreign Minister Ung Huot said on Friday that his government would discuss peace and stability with an ASEAN mission, but the grouping should not interfere in Cambodia's internal affairs.
An Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN) mediation team will arrive in Phnom Penh on Saturday to discuss peace and the political situation in the strife-torn country, Ung Huot said.

The ASEAN team will be made up of the same men who flew to Phnom Penh and tried unsuccessfully to launch a mediation effort two weeks ago -- foreign ministers Ali Alatas of Indonesia, Prachuab Chaiyasan of Thailand and Domingo Siazon of the Philippines.
But Ung Huot suggested ASEAN should not interfere in Cambodia's internal affairs.
"Does any country want other countries to interfere in its internal problems?" Ung Huot asked reporters. "Not one in the world. We are no different."
"Anything that is not interference in our internal problems we can accept," he said.

Second Prime Minster Hun Sen, who ousted his co-premier on July 6 and subsequently rejected ASEAN efforts to mediate in the crisis, will meet the three-member team on Saturday morning, an aide to Hun Sen said.
Cambodia's troubles dominated a recent ASEAN foreign ministers' meeting in Kuala Lumpur.
The grouping was thrown into confusion by conflicting signals from Cambodia over whether or not the Hun Sen-controlled government would welcome a mediation effort.
Ung Huot said in Kuala Lumpur last month that Cambodia wanted ASEAN to help mediate, but Hun Sen later said Cambodia's problems should be solved internally.
Hun Sen said ASEAN's role in ensuring Cambodia's stability should be limited to preventing foreign interference in Cambodia's affairs.
But after ASEAN requested clarification on the issue, Ung Huot wrote to the group on behalf of Hun Sen, inviting the trio of foreign ministers back to Phnom Penh for talks.
"I have the pleasure to reconfirm that Cambodia welcomes ASEAN's role to help restore political stability to the country," Ung Huot said in his letter last week.

Cambodia was scheduled to join ASEAN in late July, but the grouping postponed Cambodia's membership indefinitely in response to Hun Sen's bloody overthrow of his senior coalition partner, First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh.
ASEAN currently comprises Brunei, Burma, Indonesia, Laos, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam.
Ung Huot has been nominated by members of Ranariddh's royalist FUNCINPEC party who remained in the country after the prince's overthrow to replace him as first prime minister.
Hun Sen backs the nomination, but King Norodom Sihanouk said earlier this week he would not recognise Ung Huot's appointment as first prime minister.

Political analysts in Phnom Penh said it was not yet clear if the king's refusal to endorse Ung Huot would derail the foreign minister's nomination, but by withholding his approval, Sihanouk was clearly signalling his disapproval of Hun Sen's bloody takeover.
Meanwhile, Sihanouk expressed fears that his nation will long be the "sick man" of Asia, a Paris-based media watchdog said on Thursday.
"Alas, in Cambodia of the 1990s...recourse to armed force prevails over respect for the law," Sihanouk wrote in a letter to Reporters sans Frontieres (Reporters without Borders).

"I am very upset by such a destructive and destabilising evolution for my country, Cambodia, now considered, and I fear irredeemably for many years to come, as the 'sick man' of Asia," he wrote in a letter dated July 26 from Beijing, where he is undergoing medical treatment.
